title: Nomogram and machine learning predict 1-year mortality in sepsis cardiorenal syndrome
summary: In 340 patients with sepsis-induced cardiorenal syndrome, random forest, SVM and gradient boosted trees predicted 1-year mortality (random forest AUC 0.854); in an external cohort of 103 patients the random forest reached AUC 0.863 and the logistic nomogram 0.877, which beat SOFA (0.855 versus 0.756). The external cohort is from the same hospital in a later period, small, retrospective, and the nomogram was built by logistic regression.
ai_technology: Random forest, SVM and gradient boosted decision tree models alongside a logistic regression nomogram

evidence.tested: External cohort of 103 patients (June 2019 to December 2020) at the same hospital, compared with SOFA.
evidence.unknown: Multi-center and prospective performance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models were compared with a nomogram for predicting 1-year mortality.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
